terms.meaning: A named setting that the operating system passes to a program.
A value such as a password or API key that must not be shared or committed.
The address and name of the database the app connects to.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Settings template
sections.what: Lists the model key setting with an empty value, and the database address pointing at a local Postgres database named cartograph.
sections.why: A template records the names without values, so the structure itself carries no secret.
sections.watch_out: If the key is typed into a copy that is later committed, the key is published.

summary: A template listing the two settings the app expects: a model key and a database address. It contains no real secret values.
purpose: Shows a developer which environment settings to provide, without storing any secret.
why: Standard practice. A template tells a new clone what to set and keeps real secrets out of the repository.
how: A developer copies the file to a real environment file, fills in the key and the address, and keeps the filled copy out of version control.
inputs: None. A person reads the template.
outputs: None directly. The app reads the filled copy at startup, but that code is not in the packet.
risks: A filled copy committed by mistake would expose the key. The database address points at a local default that may not match another machine.
debug: If the app cannot reach the database, check the address and that the database is running on that port. If model calls fail, confirm the key is set in the environment.
